references.text: God's promise to Abraham that whoever blesses him will be blessed – the foundation for the idea of blessing others, even enemies.
Balaam was hired to curse Israel, but God turned the curse into a blessing – an example that God desires blessing rather than cursing.
Balaam's prophecy: "Velsignet er den som velsigner deg, forbannet er den som forbanner deg" – God's principle of blessing and cursing.
Proverbs encourages giving food and drink to one's enemy – an act of blessing toward the one who hates you.
Jesus' parallel teaching in the Sermon on the Mount: "Elsk deres fiender, velsign dem som forbanner dere, gjør godt mot dem som hater dere, og be for dem som forfølger dere."
Jesus practiced this himself on the cross when he prayed: "Far, tilgi dem, for de vet ikke hva de gjør" – a prayer for those who mistreated him.
Stephen prayed for his enemies while being stoned: "Herre, tilregn dem ikke denne synden" – an example of praying for those who persecute you.
Paul repeats Jesus' command: "Velsign dem som forfølger dere, velsign og forbann ikke."
Paul urges overcoming evil with good and giving food and drink to one's enemy – a practical expression of blessing enemies.
Paul describes his own practice: "Når vi blir forbannet, velsigner vi; når vi blir forfulgt, holder vi ut."
Peter exhorts: "Gjengjeld ikke ondt med ondt eller skjellsord med skjellsord, men velsign i stedet, for dere er kalt til å arve velsignelse."
